t: Formed from Hispania Citerior, it stretched from the Pyrenees to Galicia and was governed from Tarraco.
It held Rome's only Iberian legion, the VII Gemina at León, guarding the great gold mines of the north-west.
Split by Diocletian around 293, the reduced province was the last Roman territory in Iberia, lost to the Visigoths in the 470s.
dyk: When the people of Tarraco told Augustus that a palm tree had sprouted on his altar, he reportedly replied that this showed how often they lit fires on it, according to Quintilian.
ev: Augustus campaigns against the Cantabri and winters at Tarraco
Tiberius allows a temple to the deified Augustus at Tarraco
The governor Galba is proclaimed emperor at Carthago Nova
Bishop Fructuosus is martyred in the amphitheatre of Tarraco
Diocletian splits off Gallaecia and Carthaginiensis
Bagaudae and Suebi plunder the Ebro valley
The Visigoths under Euric take Tarraco
